intro.text: A religion tolerated in Arelon, though few Arelene converted while the Elantrians held their godlike power.
The parent religion of Shu-Korath and Shu-Dereth, centred on unity of mind and acceptance; the two sects split from it when Keseg's students disagreed on how to unite mankind.
The parent religion of Shu-Korath and Shu-Dereth, founded by Keseg, a JinDo teacher who preached the power of unity. Its teachings are kept in the Do-Kando.

description.text: Its core ideals are unity, above all unity of mind, and acceptance.
To avoid war, JinDo took up Shu-Dereth as its official religion, but most of its people still follow Shu-Keseg.
Its founder, Keseg, was a man of JinDo who preached the power of unity. Honoured as a great teacher, he was given the name KeHwo. His teachings are kept in the Do-Kando.
Shu-Keseg is still seen as the forerunner of both sects, but it is practised, unofficially, only in JinDo.

items.text: Two of Keseg's students, Korath and Dereth, left their homeland of JinDo to carry Shu-Keseg abroad, but disagreed on how to reach its central goal of unity. Korath taught that love should bring mankind together, Dereth that obedience should, and the rift produced Shu-Korath and Shu-Dereth, two rival sects.
Korath's teachings caught on in Teod, which is seen as the home of Shu-Korath.
After the fall of Fjorden's First Empire, about three centuries ago, its ruler converted to Shu-Dereth.
Fjorden then used the new faith as an excuse to conquer its neighbours in the name of divine unification, building the modern Fjordell Empire.
Arelon tolerated Shu-Keseg, but few converted while the Elantrians held their godlike power.
